units.translation: phagedaena, an ulcerous disease, on which see the passages of medical writers in Thes. vol. 8 p. 569.
a cancerous sore, which eats the flesh of my foot.
Aorist of the verb with suppletive stem ἔφαγον [I ate], I eat, I consume. In the present tense ἐσθίω [I eat] and ἤσθιον [I was eating] are used.
How could a bird be pure after eating a bird?
the one who ate the ever-living, imperishable grass.
Soon we shall know the relays of light-bearing torches.
Explained by grammarians as λαμπρός [bright] and ἰσχυρός [strong], as indicated in Thes. vol. 8 p. 577.
the tongue of a hateful dog, licking and stretching out, cheerful-minded.
the bright light of the sun.
receive the king with bright eyes and with honor.
none of the doorkeepers would receive him with a cheerful heart.
the washerwoman of the child's swaddling clothes.
Pollux 7, 40 φάιδρύνειν δὲ καὶ ἀποπλύνειν καὶ διαπλύνειν [to cleanse and to wash off and to wash thoroughly].
See similar passages in Thes. vol. 8 p. 580.
having cleansed her husband who shared her bed with baths,
the word does not cheer me.
to cleanse and to wash off and to wash thoroughly
bright-eyed, fawning at the hand and by the belly's needs.

Passive φαίνομαι [I appear] (with imperfect ἐφαινόμην [I was appearing], perfect πέφασμαι [I have appeared], first aorist ἐφάνθην [I appeared], second aorist ἐφάνην [I appeared], future φανήσομαι and φανούμαι [I will appear], and middle perfect πέφηνα [I have appeared]), I am brought to light, I appear.
With a participle, I am clear, evident.
where the manuscripts partly have φαίνοντα [showing], Nauck corrected to φανέντι [having appeared].
where I restored φαίνων [showing], after removing the gloss στρουθῶν [of sparrows]: about which I have spoken in the Preface to the fifth Leipzig edition p. LXXXVIII.

The passage is corrupt. Hermann conjectured ἀμφανεῖ [will reveal] for ἄλλα φανεῖ [will show other things] and other emendations. But nothing is gained unless the following words are emended to χρηΐζων κρυπτά [desiring hidden things]. The scholiast followed the corrupt reading, whose note is twofold: one, τὰ δὲ κρυπτὰ νῦν φανερώσει [he will now reveal the hidden things], the other θέλων πολλὰ κρυπτὰ εὑρίσκει [wishing he finds many hidden things] (thus M and the Guelferbytanus copy, not εὑρήσει [he will find], as printed).
The words are corrupt from a catalectic trochaic dimeter.
πέφανται [has appeared] is correctly read, but the reading of the remaining words is uncertain.

which the scholiast explains by τοῦ φανεροῦ [of the manifest], but recent interpreters wrongly referred it to φημί [I say], although of this verb too the participle πεφασμένος [having been said] and the imperative πεφάσθω [let it be said] exist: on which see Thes. vol. 8 p. 742.
And with the infinitive εἶναι [to be] understood.
who in the early morning, when it appears, brandishes the wing of a white-backed hawk,
showing favorable omens on the right, but also blameworthy signs,
and he will show many other things (φάνη [appeared] first hand of M, as it seems) desiring.
for he will show two forms.
let the trumpet sound an exceedingly loud cry to the army.
